title: AI Content Checklist Before You Publish | AIVideosUGC
description: A pre-publish AI content checklist for product photos and video ads: match product details, add prices yourself, and follow platform rules. Save it now.
h1: An AI Content Checklist for Product Photos and Video Ads
lead: An AI content checklist is a last look before a photo or a video goes live. You check the product, the words, and the rights to use them. AIVideosUGC can write the script, pick a presenter and a voice, and add captions (the words on screen). You still do this check before anyone sees the file.
summary: Match the product, type the price yourself, and follow each site's rule for marking an AI photo or video.

paras: This page covers what the tool makes, and how to check a photo and a clip. It also covers the price, the rights, the labels, and why shops use it. Then it covers three steps, and a comparison with booking a shoot.

sections.h2: What Is an AI Video Ad Generator?
paras: It builds a short ad from your product link, or from a line or two you type. It adds a script, a presenter, a spoken voice, and captions. You can trim the clip before it goes on your store or into an ad account.

You run this checklist on that file. Check the product against what you ship. Then check the words, the rights, and the rule on that site. A generated photo or video is a new picture made from your upload. It is not a copy of the original file. A letter in a logo can change, a button can move, an extra part can appear, or a color can shift. Use the same check on a listing photo, a social post, and a paid ad.
sections.alt: Hands check the front pocket and zipper of plain black travel backpack.

sections.h2: See What to Review on a Finished Ad
paras: Watch the file the way a shopper will, on a phone, with the sound and the captions on. Start from the first picture. The pictures below are the photos and hand shots to hold next to the real item.

Check it for the place where it will run. A [TikTok ad](page:plat-tiktok) and a [Meta ad](page:plat-facebook) both need the product to match. Meta here means Facebook and Instagram. The shape of the video can still differ. For more finished examples, start from [AI UGC video ads](page:video-ads). UGC means a clip that looks like a person filmed it on a phone. Then run the checks on this page.

sections.h2: How Do I Check AI Product Images?
paras: Hold the real item, or your original photo, next to the screen and go through color, shape, logos, parts, and size.

Compare the color in daylight, not only on a bright screen. Count the pockets, straps, and buckles. Read every letter on a label. If a hand or a familiar object is in the picture, the product should look the right size next to it. A styled scene might add a candle or a plant. Keep that extra item only when a shopper can tell it is not part of the order. Those scenes are made as [AI lifestyle product photos](page:lifestyle-photos). Count the parts there too.
sections.alt: Hands count pockets, buckles and straps on plain black travel backpack.

sections.h2: What Is on an AI Video Review Checklist?
paras: Play the clip on your phone. Listen to the voice, and read the captions. Then go through it slowly. Watch the hands and the first picture.

The script should name the product you ship. Do not mention a feature that is not for sale. Clips often go wrong while the product moves. A label can blur as it turns. Fingers can blend into a strap. A zipper can change shape halfway through. Count the fingers, and watch how they hold the item. The first picture often becomes the thumbnail, the small preview shoppers see first. If one short moment looks wrong, trim it in the editor on this site. If the problem runs through the whole clip, make a new version. Run this same check on an [AI product video generator](page:product-videos) clip before you post it.
sections.alt: Hands open the zipper and flap of plain black travel backpack.

sections.h2: Which Checks Should I Do Before I Publish the Price?
paras: Make the picture or the clip first. Then add the price, the date, the code, and the headline yourself.

Do not ask the tool to write those words inside the image or the clip. Letters the tool draws are often wrong or messy. Captions can follow what is spoken. You still type the price, the date, and the code yourself. Every character should match the product page. Before you post, match the price and the code to the store. Check that any end date is still ahead. If stray letters show on a package or a sign, remove that part of the picture or try again.
sections.alt: Plain black travel backpack centered on a white background.

sections.h2: What Do I Need to Own Before an AI Ad Goes Live?
paras: Upload only photos you took, or photos you have permission to use. Use only logos that belong to you.

If the photo comes from a supplier, your agreement with them must cover ads. A request built around another company's logo, or a celebrity, may be refused. The [Content Policy](/content) says what you can upload. For music, pick a song from the music library, the song list on this site. Or use a track you already licensed for ads. The presenter and the voice you pick are for the ads you make on AIVideosUGC.
sections.alt: Hands hold plain black travel backpack beside a plain camera and blank phone.

sections.h2: When Do AI-Generated Content Labels Apply?
paras: Read the current rule on each site you post to. Several sites ask you to mark a realistic generated person or scene. That rule can change.

Keep two rules on every site. Do not show a generated person as a real customer or reviewer. That includes [AI model photos for clothing](page:model-photos). Do not let a caption promise a health, skin, or weight result. Show how the product is used, and let the shopper decide.

sections.h2: Reasons to Use AIVideosUGC for a Video Ad
paras: The script starts from your product page, or from the lines you type. The opening is about the item you sell.

The file comes out in a shape that fits a phone feed, a square post, or a product page. Those shapes are listed on [pricing](page:pricing). 9:16 is a tall phone video. 1:1 is a square. 16:9 is a wide video. 3:4 is a little taller than it is wide.
From one photo, you can get more than one presenter, opening line, or tone. Keep the version that fits the shop. Save the other versions.

paras: Turn the photo into a [product video](page:product-videos). Or start from the [video tools](page:video-hub) if you are still choosing a format.
A clip of a presenter talking about the product is on [AI UGC video ads](page:video-ads). A post for the feed can follow [Instagram ads](page:plat-instagram).

If the photo should simply start to move, use [image to video](page:image-to-video). Then run this checklist.

Timing. You upload a photo or paste a link, then review a clip. You do not have to book a day with a crew.

Next product. The next item uses the same steps. You do not wait on one person's calendar.

sections.h2: How Shops Use a Checked Video Ad
paras: A skincare shop shows a presenter holding the bottle and saying what is in it. Then a person checks that label against the real bottle.
A gadget shop opens the box on a desk and confirms every part in the kit is the part that ships.
A clothing shop shows the piece on an adult, then matches the neckline and the print to the sample.
A food shop sets the jar on a counter, and the voice names the flavor printed on the lid.
A candle shop lets hands lift the lid, and the caption follows that one motion.
A jewelry shop turns the piece once, and a person counts the stones before the file is posted.
A shop with buyers in two countries keeps the same presenter and speaks the script in the other language.
A two-person team makes the next opening line from the photo they already checked, instead of booking another afternoon.
A marketplace seller pastes the listing link, then fixes any line that does not match the live product page.
A shop testing two opening lines keeps both clips and posts one. It holds the other until the first clip has played.

Build the ad from a link, or from a short note you type. You get a script, a presenter, a voice, and captions. Then match the product, and type the price yourself. Use only photos, logos, and music you have the rights to use.
Send it to TikTok or Meta, or download it with no watermark, only after those checks. If a shopper could feel misled, do not post that file.

faq.q: What does an AI video ad generator make?
faq.a: A short ad made from your product link, or from lines you type. It has a script, a presenter, a voice, and captions. You still check the product, the words, and the rights before it goes live.

faq.q: How do I create a video ad with AI?
faq.a: Paste your product link, or describe the item. Review the draft script and the presenter. Then download the video, or send it to TikTok or Meta.

faq.q: What should the finished ad include?
faq.a: Name the product you actually ship. Use a presenter you are willing to mark as generated. Add a voice, and captions for what is spoken. Use a video shape the place you post already accepts.

faq.q: What should I check before posting an AI-made video?
faq.a: Watch it on your phone, from the first picture to the last. Check the product, the hands, the label, the voice, and the captions. Then check that any price you added matches the store.

faq.q: What if an extra object looks like it comes with the order?
faq.a: Do not use that version, or say clearly in the listing what is included. Decoration is fine only when a shopper would not expect it in the box.

faq.q: Can I ask the tool to draw my discount code?
faq.a: No. Add the code, the price, and the date yourself after you download, so the letters stay correct. Captions can follow what is spoken. They do not replace the price or the code.

faq.q: Do I have to say a person is generated?
faq.a: Check the current rule for each platform or marketplace you use. Do not describe a generated person as a real customer, even where the site lets you mark the ad as generated.

faq.q: Can I use a supplier photo as the source?
faq.a: Only if your agreement with the supplier covers ads. Otherwise shoot your own photo.

faq.q: What if one moment in the clip looks wrong?
faq.a: Trim that moment in the editor if it is brief. If the error runs through the clip, make a new version instead of posting it.

faq.q: Can I publish the file to TikTok or Meta from here?
faq.a: Yes. Meta means Facebook and Instagram. After you finish the checks, send the file to TikTok or Meta. Or download it with no watermark, meaning no logo on the file, and upload it yourself.
